Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Soreness, cracking, and dryness of the skin on the hands, primarily palms and fingers.
  - Patient works as a hotel housekeeper using cleaning products and reports inconsistent use of gloves; symptoms began after job change ~3–4 months ago and patient believes exposure to cleaning products is the likely trigger.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset ~3–4 months ago after job change.
  - Gradual worsening; more painful recently such that patient has been unable to work for the past 3 days.
  - Intermittent itching; occasional bleeding after scratching.
- ENT symptoms:
  - No throat tightness or closing sensation reported.
  - No voice change/hoarseness.
  - No dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal or ocular symptoms.
  - No stridor/noisy breathing or dyspnea.
  - No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling reported.
  - No ear pain, hearing changes, or neck pain/swelling reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior diagnosed skin conditions reported.
  - Patient tried E45 emollient — ineffective.
  - Patient tried an antihistamine — ineffective (name/dose not documented).
  - No prior ED visits, hospitalizations, or injection therapy for this issue reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - No known allergies reported.
  - Current medication: metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Planned prescriptions: topical steroid cream (type/dose/route/frequency not documented) and “stronger emollient” (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social context:
  - Works as a hotel housekeeper, recent job change ~4 months ago.
  - Reports inconsistent glove use at work.
  - Non-smoker. Alcohol: a couple of pints per week.
  - Off work for 3 days due to symptoms.
  - No mention of accompaniment or supervision during consult.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: No swelling documented. Patient-reported cracked, sore skin of palms/fingers; no clinician physical exam findings recorded.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Not recorded; patient denied breathing or throat symptoms.
- Mental status and associated features: Patient alert, coherent; no dizziness or syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Primary impression: Likely irritant/contact dermatitis (occupational), consistent with:
  - Onset/progression after change to housekeeping role using cleaning products.
  - History of inadequate glove use.
  - Chronic dry, cracked, itchy palms with pain and occasional bleeding after scratching.
- Differential/uncertainty:
  - Contact dermatitis vs. other dermatitis types; no diagnostic testing or specialist assessment documented.
  - No conflicting statements in transcript.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Prescription to be issued and sent to patient’s pharmacy (topical steroid cream — type/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Advise use of a stronger emollient, to apply approximately 3–4 times daily as discussed (specific product/dose not documented).
  - Advice to avoid triggers: wear gloves when cleaning at all times.
- Specific instructions to patient:
  - Apply emollients regularly (coat on 3–4 times daily).
  - Use gloves for cleaning to reduce exposure to irritants.
  - Return for review if no improvement or if symptoms worsen.
  - Prescription will be sent to the pharmacy.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (as discussed):
  - Return sooner if condition is getting worse, spreading, or not improved.
- Follow-up:
  - Review in clinic if no improvement in ~1–2 weeks (doctor suggested 10–14 days) or sooner if worsening.
  - Consider further management options if insufficient response at follow-up (not specified).
- Other:
  - No discussion of auto-injector, allergy testing, occupational health referral, or emergency contact instructions in transcript.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented physical examination findings of the hands (inspection, distribution, severity).
  - No vitals recorded.
  - Exact topical steroid name, potency, dose, route and duration not documented.
  - Exact emollient product and instructions beyond frequency not documented.
  - No occupational health referral or advice on specific glove type/material.
  - No documented plan for patch testing or dermatology referral if persistent.
  - No documentation of prior anaphylaxis history or availability of auto-injector (relevant for allergy presentations; patient reported no allergies).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Transcript is clear and complete for the consultation content relevant to the skin complaint; occasional hesitations present but overall intelligible.
